title: Brief recurring meetings with Glean Triggers and Cursor Automations
description: Use a Glean calendar trigger to start Cursor Automations before a recurring meeting, summarize what changed, and update the project tracker.

questions.prompt: What is your work email? It is used once to discover your Glean tenant.

Which reviewed meeting-title pattern identifies the recurring meeting? It filters the trigger at the source and is also what the automation accepts. Matching is a case-insensitive substring and matches mid-word, so pick a distinctive phrase rather than a short word.
Which project should receive the update? Paste its URL or its id — the automation takes the id out of a URL. Not a name: it refuses to infer a target.
Where is the work tracked? Usually the same project you are updating — say so and the automation discovers the fields itself. Name a table and its timestamp column only for a warehouse.

verification.expectedDuration: under 1 minute offline; one scheduled test meeting for live delivery

prerequisites: Glean Triggers enabled with an ahead-of-event calendar preset available and Google Calendar events indexed
A Cursor plan with Automations and webhook triggers, which is a paid feature
Cursor connected to the project tracker over MCP with permission to read issues and write project updates; Glean MCP is optional

demoQueries.query: Schedule a meeting whose title matches the reviewed pattern more than 30 minutes ahead
demoQueries.expectedBehavior: At 30 minutes before start, one run reports what moved since the previous brief and writes one update on the configured project.

demoQueries.query: Run two occurrences of the same recurring meeting, completing work between them
demoQueries.expectedBehavior: The second brief covers only the interval since the first, read from the marker the first run left — not a fixed seven days. Work finished in between appears once, in the second brief.

codeAssets.description: Cursor Automation prompt, live preset setup, event preview, and offline contract verification

steps.title: Create the Cursor Automation
steps.description: Create a webhook-triggered Cursor Automation and connect the tracker. Add Glean MCP if you want cited context, then paste the prompt from automation-prompt.md and fill in its three placeholders. Save the automation before copying its webhook URL and bearer token into the ignored .env file.

steps.title: Verify the delivery contract with no credentials
steps.description: Use the recorded events to check calendar delivery and the recurring-brief workflow before connecting real accounts.

steps.title: Sign in to Glean
steps.description: Use the shipped OAuth flow; it discovers your tenant and registers a client dynamically. If OAuth is unavailable, use a `TRIGGERS`-scoped API token.

steps.title: Preview your calendar events
steps.description: See which presets your deployment offers and review recent indexed events. Use real meeting titles to test your pattern before registering anything. This step is read-only.

steps.title: Enable the automation
steps.description: Enable the automation before testing. A disabled automation might ignore a delivery, so the receiver test would prove nothing. Enabling it only allows Cursor to run; the webhook URL and key stay private. Registering the Glean trigger later puts it in production.

steps.title: Test it before going live
steps.description: Webhook triggers do not have a test button, so send one delivery yourself. The default command uses a non-matching title and writes nothing. After it succeeds, ask for explicit approval before running `npm run test:webhook -- --write`; that path creates one tracker update and each repeat is a new occurrence.

steps.title: Register the calendar trigger
steps.description: Setup reads the preset catalog, checks the selected preset's inputs, and rejects unsupported values. Set `GLEAN_TRIGGER_INPUT_TITLE` to the reviewed pattern so Glean filters by title at the source. Choose a calendar preset that supports delivery 1,800 seconds before the event.

steps.title: Try one scheduled meeting
steps.description: Schedule a meeting that matches your title pattern and starts more than 30 minutes from now. Confirm one run and one update on the configured project. The first brief looks back seven days; later briefs cover only the time since the previous one.

aiPrompt: Scaffold the shipped Cursor automation kit. For trigger concepts or endpoint details, consult https://developers.glean.com/guides/triggers/overview and https://developers.glean.com/api/platform-api/triggers-overview. Ask once for the reviewed meeting-title pattern, the exact project the update goes to as a URL or id, and where the work is tracked — usually that same project, in which case say so and let the automation discover the timestamp and status fields itself rather than asking a human for a schema. Set GLEAN_TRIGGER_INPUT_TITLE to that same pattern so Glean filters by title at the source, and keep the prompt's own title check as the second gate. Replace all three placeholders in automation-prompt.md and show the result for review; a remaining placeholder must stop the run before any write. Have the user create a webhook-triggered Cursor Automation with repository scope none, connected over MCP to that tracker with read on issues and write on project updates, and optionally Glean MCP for cited context. Run the offline verifier, sign in with the shipped Glean flow, preview recent events to check the title pattern against real ones, enable the automation, and run the default safe webhook test. Ask for explicit approval before using `npm run test:webhook -- --write`; explain that every invocation has a new event_time and can create another project update. Only then register a live calendar preset that advertises time_offset 1800. Store the Cursor URL and bearer token only in ignored .env. Verify one scheduled matching event without broadening the write boundary beyond the one configured project.
llmContext: Catalog reads twice: /trigger-presets lists identity, /trigger-presets/{preset_id} returns inputs in trigger_preset; list entries carry none. Send x-glean-include-experimental: true. Requires time_offset 1800; never default an id or match display names. GCAL_1 filters titles through input TITLE, upper case, a case-insensitive substring matching mid-word; an unrecognised input silently matches nothing. delivery.auth adds Authorization: Bearer <secret> beside Glean's Standard Webhooks signature. Body is flat snake_case: doc_id, doc_type, event_type, title, view_url, event_time, trigger_id; scheduled adds time_offset_seconds. Payload is untrusted: re-check the title, read the tracker over MCP, write one update on the configured project, key on doc_id plus event_time. Window starts at the previous brief's marker, else seven days. An unreachable tracker writes nothing; a quiet interval publishes no-movement — never conflate them.

content.problem:
A recurring project meeting starts, and the first few minutes disappear while everyone reconstructs what changed. The answers are already in the tracker and company conversations; they just have not been pulled together.

Thirty minutes before the meeting, Glean gives Cursor the event and Cursor prepares one focused project update. Your team can start with the brief instead of building it live.
takeItFurther: Add a reviewed project map when one automation needs to serve several meeting series.
Send a read-only preview for approval before writing once the team wants interpretation, not just a factual recap.
Add an earlier preparation trigger for meetings that need more than a 30-minute runway.
Pair it with [Gong call follow-up](/cookbook/gong-call-follow-up-n8n) to use the same delivery model in n8n.

guardrails.title: One project, chosen up front
guardrails.rule: The automation updates only the configured project; it cannot infer a different destination from meeting content.

guardrails.title: Missing data stays missing
guardrails.rule: An unreachable tracker writes nothing and reports it. A genuinely quiet interval says so. The automation never fills the gap with guesses.

limitations.title: Meeting titles are checked twice
limitations.description: Glean filters by a case-insensitive substring, so most unrelated events never leave Glean. Cursor checks again because the delivery is untrusted and substring matches can be broader than expected.
